turns.utterance: Complete the following checks: First, inspect the electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than one millimeter or any mushrooming. Second, check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. Third, inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than 1 mm or mushrooming. 2. Check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. 3. Inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've completed all three checks. The electrode caps show some minor wear but no deep pitting or mushrooming, the shank surfaces are clean, and both coolant ports are clear.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than 1 mm or mushrooming. 2. Check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. 3. Inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the caps are in acceptable condition. There's no severe damage, deep pitting, mushrooming, or cracking present.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Electrode face diameter within wear limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode face diameter within wear limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, I've checked the measurements and the face diameter is still within the acceptable wear limit for both electrodes.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode face diameter within wear limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

ground_truth.node_text: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, both electrodes are showing flow rates above the minimum specification. The cooling system is functioning properly.

ground_truth.node_text: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Electrode force within plus or minus five percent of programmed schedule value?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode force within ±5% of programmed schedule value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured force is reading about eight percent below the programmed value. It's outside the tolerance band.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode force within ±5% of programmed schedule value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the pneumatic pressure regulator on the electrode arm to bring the force back into specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pneumatic pressure regulator on electrode arm

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've adjusted the regulator and increased the pneumatic pressure to compensate for the low force reading.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pneumatic pressure regulator on electrode arm

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The force is now within tolerance. The adjustment brought it back to within three percent of the programmed value.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Measured weld current within plus or minus three percent of scheduled value?

ground_truth.node_text: Measured weld current within ±3% of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the peak current is reading about five percent low compared to the scheduled value on the test weld.

ground_truth.node_text: Measured weld current within ±3% of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Access the weld controller parameter menu using the maintenance password, read the current correction factor for the affected welding schedule, and compare the stored factor against the reference value for this material stack.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following steps: 1. Access the weld controller parameter menu using the maintenance password. 2. Read the current correction factor for the affected welding schedule. 3. Compare the stored factor against the reference value for this material stack.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've accessed the controller and reviewed the correction factor. I can see it needs adjustment to match the reference value.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following steps: 1. Access the weld controller parameter menu using the maintenance password. 2. Read the current correction factor for the affected welding schedule. 3. Compare the stored factor against the reference value for this material stack.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify weld current after controller correction.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify weld current after controller correction

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The current is now reading within specification. The correction brought it to within two percent of the scheduled value.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify weld current after controller correction

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Weld time within plus or minus one cycle of scheduled value?

ground_truth.node_text: Weld time within ±1 cycle of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured weld time is running about two cycles longer than the programmed schedule.

ground_truth.node_text: Weld time within ±1 cycle of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the weld timer setting in the controller schedule to correct the timing deviation.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld timer setting in controller schedule

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Timer adjustment complete. I've reduced the cycle count to bring it back to the scheduled value.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld timer setting in controller schedule

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at twenty-five percent of the programmed force setting and open. Inspect the carbon transfer pattern on each face for concentricity and coverage.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at 25% of the programmed force setting and open. Inspect the carbon transfer pattern on each face; the contact impression should be concentric and cover the full electrode face area uniformly. An off centre or crescent shaped pattern indicates electrode misalignment requiring mechanical correction.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've completed the carbon transfer test. The pattern shows good contact impression on both faces.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at 25% of the programmed force setting and open. Inspect the carbon transfer pattern on each face; the contact impression should be concentric and cover the full electrode face area uniformly. An off centre or crescent shaped pattern indicates electrode misalignment requiring mechanical correction.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Electrode faces parallel, contact pattern above ninety percent of face area?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode faces parallel, contact pattern above 90% of face area?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the electrodes are parallel and the contact pattern covers well over ninety percent of the face area. The impression is uniform and concentric.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode faces parallel, contact pattern above 90% of face area?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Pilot weld appearance, no spatter, expulsion or surface cracks?

ground_truth.node_text: Pilot weld appearance, no spatter, expulsion or surface cracks?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, I'm seeing some spatter around the weld zone and minor surface irregularities on a couple of the test specimens.

ground_truth.node_text: Pilot weld appearance, no spatter, expulsion or surface cracks?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the weld schedule and modify current and force parameters for this material batch to eliminate the spatter.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld schedule, modify current and force for material batch

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've made adjustments to the schedule, reducing the current slightly and optimizing the force profile for this batch.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld schedule, modify current and force for material batch

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Apply ultrasonic couplant to the electrode face side of each pilot weld coupon and scan the weld zone using an A scan ultrasonic probe. Record the reflected signal amplitude and identify the nugget boundary to measure the nugget diameter.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply ultrasonic couplant to the electrode face side of each pilot weld coupon and scan the weld zone using an A scan ultrasonic probe. Record the reflected signal amplitude and the back wall echo attenuation. Identify the nugget boundary and measure the nugget diameter from the scan image. Compare against the minimum nugget diameter in the weld quality specification.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Ultrasonic scanning complete. I've recorded the signal data and measured the nugget diameters from the scan images.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply ultrasonic couplant to the electrode face side of each pilot weld coupon and scan the weld zone using an A scan ultrasonic probe. Record the reflected signal amplitude and the back wall echo attenuation. Identify the nugget boundary and measure the nugget diameter from the scan image. Compare against the minimum nugget diameter in the weld quality specification.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Weld nugget diameter meets minimum for material thickness?

ground_truth.node_text: Weld nugget diameter meets minimum for material thickness?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, all measured nugget diameters are above the minimum specification for this material thickness.

ground_truth.node_text: Weld nugget diameter meets minimum for material thickness?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Peel test shows button pull failure mode, no interfacial fracture?

ground_truth.node_text: Peel test shows button pull failure mode, no interfacial fracture?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, all the peel tests produced clean button pull failures. The nuggets pulled out completely with no interfacial fractures observed.

ground_truth.node_text: Peel test shows button pull failure mode, no interfacial fracture?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Weld controller backup completed successfully?

ground_truth.node_text: Weld controller backup completed successfully?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the backup transfer completed without errors and I've verified the file on the server with the current timestamp.

ground_truth.node_text: Weld controller backup completed successfully?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Coolant return temperature within rated range?

ground_truth.node_text: Coolant return temperature within rated range?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the return line temperature is running about five degrees above the maximum rated temperature at steady state.

ground_truth.node_text: Coolant return temperature within rated range?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Check the chiller setpoint and clean the condenser to bring the coolant temperature back into range.

ground_truth.node_text: Check chiller setpoint and clean condenser

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've verified the chiller setpoint and cleaned the condenser coils. Temperature should stabilize now.

ground_truth.node_text: Check chiller setpoint and clean condenser

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Run twenty consecutive production welds at the standard schedule settings with the machine in normal production configuration. Log the weld current, force, and time for each weld, then inspect the final five weld spots visually.

ground_truth.node_text: Run 20 consecutive production welds at the standard schedule settings with the machine in normal production configuration. Log the weld current, weld force, and weld time for each weld from the controller weld data output. Inspect the final five weld spots visually for consistent button size and absence of surface expulsion before signing off the qualification record.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've completed the twenty production qualification welds and logged all the data. The weld spots have been inspected.

ground_truth.node_text: Run 20 consecutive production welds at the standard schedule settings with the machine in normal production configuration. Log the weld current, weld force, and weld time for each weld from the controller weld data output. turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: All production qualification welds within specification?

ground_truth.node_text: All production qualification welds within specification?

ground_truth.node_text: All production qualification welds within specification?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: This procedure must be escalated. The persistent qualification failures indicate a metallurgical issue requiring engineering review. Do not return this equipment to production until a weld engineer has completed a full assessment.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Escalate: peel test failure persistent, metallurgical review

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll tag the machine out and notify the weld engineering team for metallurgical review.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Escalate: peel test failure persistent, metallurgical review
